steps.title: Divide
steps.body:
$$\frac{\alpha^n+\beta^n}{\alpha^{-n}+\beta^{-n}} = (\alpha^n+\beta^n)\cdot\frac{(\alpha\beta)^n}{\alpha^n+\beta^n} = (\alpha\beta)^n = 4^n$$
The answer is **B**.

optionAnalysis.reason: $n^4$ swaps base and exponent; the result is $(\alpha\beta)^n$.
The ratio equals $(\alpha\beta)^n = 4^n$.

cse-2016-2-cs-1.approach: Simplify the premise: $P \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q) \equiv P \wedge Q$ (modus ponens). Then a formula is implied iff it is true whenever $P = Q = \text{true}$.

steps.title: Simplify the premise
steps.body: $P \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q) = P \wedge (\neg P \vee Q) = (P \wedge \neg P) \vee (P \wedge Q) = P \wedge Q$. It is true only when $P = Q = T$.

steps.title: Evaluate each expression at P = Q = T
steps.body:
| Expression | Value | Implied? |
|---|---|---|
| (i) false | F | No |
| (ii) $Q$ | T | Yes |
| (iii) true | T | Yes |
| (iv) $P \vee Q$ | T | Yes |
| (v) $\neg Q \vee P$ | F ∨ T = T | Yes |

steps.title: Count
steps.body: Expressions (ii), (iii), (iv), (v) are implied: **4**.

pitfalls: Counting 'false' as implied: only a contradictory premise implies false, and $P \wedge Q$ is satisfiable.
cse-2016-2-cs-1.verification: The premise has exactly one satisfying assignment (P = Q = T); four of the five expressions are true there.

cse-2016-2-cs-2.approach: $f(x)+f(-x)$ keeps only the even-power terms of $f$, and $g(x)-g(-x)$ keeps only the odd-power terms of $g = f'$, which come from differentiating those even-power terms.
concepts: Even and odd parts of a polynomial

steps.title: What the given degree says
steps.body: Let $f(x) = \sum a_k x^k$. Then $f(x)+f(-x) = 2\sum_{k \text{ even}} a_k x^k$. Degree 10 means $a_{10} \ne 0$ and $a_k = 0$ for every even $k > 10$ (odd terms of $f$ may be of any degree).

steps.title: Odd part of g
steps.body: $g(x) = f'(x) = \sum k a_k x^{k-1}$. Then $g(x)-g(-x) = 2\sum_{k-1 \text{ odd}} k a_k x^{k-1}$, i.e. the terms coming from **even** $k$.

steps.title: Its degree
steps.body: The largest even $k$ with $a_k \ne 0$ is $10$, giving the term $2 \cdot 10 a_{10} x^{9} \ne 0$. So the degree of $g(x)-g(-x)$ is **9**.

pitfalls: Assuming $\deg f = 10$; $f$ may contain higher odd powers, but they do not affect $g(x)-g(-x)$.

cse-2016-2-cs-4.approach: Test each statement with a small counterexample or witness: an inconsistent underdetermined system kills I, a homogeneous system kills II, and the identity system proves III.

steps.title: Statement I (m < n)
steps.body: Take $m = 2, n = 3$: $x+y+z = 1$ and $x+y+z = 2$. The two equations contradict each other, so this system has no solution. **I is false.**

steps.title: Statement II (m > n)
steps.body: Any homogeneous system $Ax = 0$ has the solution $x = 0$, whatever $m$ and $n$ are; e.g. $m = 3, n = 2$: $x = 0, y = 0, x + y = 0$. **II is false.**

steps.title: Statement III (m = n)
steps.body: The system $Ix = b$ (identity matrix) has the solution $x = b$. A system with a solution exists, so **III is true**. Only III holds: answer **C**.

optionAnalysis.reason: I and II both have counterexamples.
II is false: homogeneous overdetermined systems always have the zero solution.
III is an existence claim, witnessed by $Ix = b$; I and II are false.
III is true.

cse-2016-2-cs-4.verification: Rank view: a system is consistent iff $\text{rank}(A) = \text{rank}([A\mid b])$, which depends on the entries, not only on $m$ vs $n$; so 'all' (I) and 'none' (II) both fail, while 'there exists' (III) holds.

cse-2016-2-cs-7.approach: The worst ripple-carry delay happens when a carry generated at bit 0 must propagate through every higher stage, i.e. every bit of B is 1 (each stage has $A_i \oplus B_i = 1$ above bit 0).

steps.title: A in binary
steps.body: $A = 1 = 0000\,0001_2$. Bit 0 is the only bit where a carry can be **generated** ($A_0 B_0 = 1$ needs $B_0 = 1$).

steps.title: Make the carry ripple all the way
steps.body:
For bits 1–7, $A_i = 0$, so the carry propagates through stage $i$ only if $B_i = 1$. Choosing $B_i = 1$ for every bit makes the carry from bit 0 pass through all 8 stages:
$$0000\,0001 + 1111\,1111 = (1)\,0000\,0000$$

steps.title: Decimal value of B
steps.body: $B = 1111\,1111_2$ in 2's complement is $-1$. So the answer is **−1**.

cse-2016-2-cs-7.verification: Any B with a 0 in some bit $i \ge 1$ stops the carry at stage $i$; B with $B_0 = 0$ generates no carry at all. Only $B = 11111111 = -1$ gives the full 8-stage ripple.
